title: own scope targeting its declared owned Entity — the legitimate case
why: The Action declares scope 'own', names 'Widget' as its target, 'Widget' is declared in this manifest, and 'Widget' declares ownershipField 'created_by' — which is itself a declared field on that entity. Every link in the chain resolves. This is what an App legitimately doing owner-scoped access looks like, and it must install. A validator that cannot accept this one is not enforcing AZ7, it is refusing 'own' entirely.
notes: MUST BE ACCEPTED BY BOTH LAYERS. This is the primary over-rejection guard for the whole AZ7 set. Any schema amendment or validator rule that rejects az7-n4 must still accept this fixture; if both fail, the implementation is broken in the opposite direction and the failure is a defect against the implementer, not against the fixture. Note also that ownershipField 'created_by' names a field that actually appears in entities[0].fields — that the ownershipField must name a real field on its own entity is a further validator obligation, and az7-q2 records it as an open question rather than assuming it.
